line.text: Every tax in your Budget, one notch up, ranked by what the figures say it raises. HMRC’s and the Treasury’s figures where they exist; our own arithmetic, badged, where they do not. The ones that break a promise say so.

Everything in your package that costs money, biggest first. A measure that starts a year later costs nothing in the years before it starts; the OBR scores what is in the forecast window and the department feels the wait.
Half the distance to the target is still a real change to a real budget. It is also half a promise, and the Prime Minister will notice which half.

Lowering the target costs nothing today; the markets never saw it. They see the number: Budget 2025 left £21.7bn, the OBR’s typical five-year error is about £32bn, and the Bank found this year’s gilt moves amplified by hedge fund deleveraging.

The Charter lets a Chancellor suspend the rules in a significant shock, judged by the OBR. A rule missed by choice is not that; the OBR will say so on Budget day. Nothing stops you. Write down that you know.

noBreach.text: No rule is missed on these numbers. Leaving the gap open is not a breach; it is less headroom than you meant to keep, and the target is yours to lower if you can live with that.
